subject: Retention boundaries: concrete examples for requests, prompts, and model outputs
messages:
From: DataOps - Acme Corp <dataops@acme.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: security@bigbank.com
Date: 2028-03-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Clarify what Redwood keeps by default (examples attached)

Hi Mina / Marissa,

We're completing our vendor security review and need to be precise about what Redwood retains by default for hosted customers. We've attached a small CSV sample of API calls from our staging traffic (acme-sample-logs.csv). Two specific scenarios:

1) A user prompt that includes a customer name and order ID. Does Redwood persist the raw prompt text, tokenized request, or both?
2) A separate run where the model output contains derived account numbers and a remediation suggestion. Is that output considered "stored artifact" or ephemeral?

Also, what are the deletion guarantees if we ask for a purge of those rows? We need exact timelines and the API/process to trigger deletion so we can document it for our auditors.

Thanks — appreciate a concrete example-based answer.

Best,
Jared Lopez
DataOps Manager, Acme Corp
attachments: acme-sample-logs.csv

From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
To: DataOps - Acme Corp <dataops@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-01T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify what Redwood keeps by default (examples attached)

Hi Jared — thanks for the examples, this is helpful. High-level answers first, then a short actionable checklist below.

High-level: by default our hosted offering differentiates three buckets: request metadata, request content (prompts), and model-generated outputs. Retention and handling differ by bucket. For hosted customers the out-of-the-box defaults are conservative to support troubleshooting and quality monitoring while balancing privacy.

Quick checklist (concrete):
- Request metadata (timestamps, API key id, route, token counts): retained 30 days by default; aggregated metrics kept longer.
- Raw prompts (text you sent): retained 90 days by default for quality/regression analysis unless you enable the "do_not_store" option at request time or you have an enterprise contract that sets a different policy.
- Model outputs (text generated): treated as artifacts and retained 90 days by default; flagged outputs containing high-risk PII are subject to accelerated purge once identified.

Deletion: we provide a deletion API (POST /v1/tenants/{id}/purge) that accepts selectors (time range, API key, request id). Standard hosted purge jobs complete within 48 hours for indexed items; complete physical purge from backups within 30 days (we document the backup retention SLA). For compliance customers we can accelerate the backup purge through an elevated process (see attached retention-table.csv).

I'll follow up with exact examples mapping to the rows in your CSV. If you need a formal SOC2 evidence pack, we can share the artifacts in the SOC2-evidence.pdf link.

—Mina
Mina Haddad
Senior Security Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks Mina — that's clearer. A follow-up: one of our rows shows the prompt that included a legacy customer SSN field which we redacted post-hoc. In that scenario, is the prompt still retained in the 90-day store (with redaction applied), or does Redwood keep an immutable raw copy for debugging?

(Quoted for context)

> > High-level: by default our hosted offering differentiates three buckets: request metadata, request content (prompts), and model-generated outputs. Retention and handling differ by bucket.

Also, the output in one row includes an account number that looks like it could match production. If we request a targeted purge for that request id, will the matching output be removed from the retention index and any downstream analytic stores?

Appreciate specifics so we can close this out with our auditors.

—Jared

From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
To: DataOps - Acme Corp <dataops@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-03T17:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify what Redwood keeps by default (examples attached)

Hi Jared — answers mapped to your two concrete scenarios and next steps below.

Scenario A — prompt with legacy SSN (your CSV row #4):
- Default behavior: we store the raw prompt string in the "prompt store" for 90 days to support model quality and debugging. That raw copy is the exact payload you POSTed (no additional unmasking happens on our side).
- If you redact after the fact: our purge API can remove the indexed prompt and any derived tokenized traces tied to that request id. The indexed item is unsearchable within 48 hours; full cryptographic/backup removal follows the backup retention SLA (default 30 days).
- If you require non-retention of prompts up-front: include header X-Redwood-Store: false (or use the SDK flag store=false) and the request will be treated as non-persistent (no prompt or output is written to the long-term stores). This is available to all hosted customers by default.

Scenario B — model output with account number (CSV row #9):
- Outputs are kept in the artifact store for 90 days by default. When you call the purge API with the request id we: 1) remove the artifact from the active index within 48 hours, 2) remove any downstream analytic copies (metrics & alerts) within 72 hours, and 3) schedule backup removal.
- For high-risk PII, we offer an expedited deletion flow for enterprise customers that completes offline backup deletion within 7–14 days. Request this via your account manager (Marissa is cc'd).

Additional items / controls:
- Audit trail: purge requests are logged and we can provide signed attestations for each purge operation.
- Private & Dedicated customers: you control retention via tenant config (shorter retention or permanent disablement available behind contract).
- Operability: if you want to prevent any accidental capture during red-team exercises, use store=false on the request and we will not persist prompt text or outputs beyond transient runtime memory.

Attachments referenced: retention-table.csv (default timelines and escalation windows) and SOC2-evidence.pdf (audit artifacts we can share under NDA).

Recommended next steps:
1) If you want a targeted purge now, reply with the request ids (or time window) and we will open a purge job.
2) If you need a formal statement for your audit, we will produce a signed purge attestation + timeline.

Marissa / Neha — I recommend we open the enterprise escalation for accelerated backup purge if Acme requests it. Marissa, can you confirm SLAs/fees? Neha, can you prepare the attestation template?

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if that helps.

—Mina
